name: Boontjiesop
summary: Bean soup: dried sugar beans simmered with a meaty beef shin and vegetables until thick and velvety, the Karoo's winter soup in a bowl.
about: Boontjiesop is Afrikaans for bean soup, and a version of it appears in South African household guides from the early 1900s. Farm kitchens in the Karoo made it from dried beans and whatever bones or smoked pork were on hand, and it is still the soup of cold evenings, filling enough to be the whole meal.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: add after the beans are soft

steps: Drain and rinse the soaked beans and set them aside.
Heat the oil in a large soup pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef shin slices for about 3 minutes a side, until well coloured.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions, carrots and celery and fry, stirring, until the onions are soft, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the beans, bay leaves and water. Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, lower the heat and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring every now and then, until the beans are soft and the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer, half-covered, for another 30 minutes, until the potatoes are falling apart and the soup has thickened.
Lift out the shin, pull the meat off the bones, chop it and return it to the pot. Throw away the bones and bay leaves.
Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pot with a potato masher to make the soup thick and creamy. If it is too thick, add a cup of boiling water.
Season with the salt, pepper and lemon juice, simmer for 5 more minutes, then stir in the parsley and serve hot.
prepNote: Soak the beans the night before. The soup keeps 3 days in the fridge and thickens as it stands; loosen with water.
